title: Stakeholder Status Matrix and Callout Protocol
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines the stakeholder status matrix, callout and escalation protocol, on-call succession rules, and standardized status-page and customer communication templates for all multi-service incidents affecting Redwood Inference. It consolidates the lifecycle from first detection -> bridge -> customer notice -> postmortem archival, and prescribes time-boxed SLAs for each phase.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce confusion in cross-functional incidents by clarifying who is notified, when, and how, and providing pre-approved message templates for public (customer-facing) and private (internal/legal) channels.
- Scope: Applies to all incidents with potential customer impact for Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Excludes internal-only tooling outages without customer visibility (see "service impact tiers").

Key contacts and ownership:
- Incident Commander (IC): service owner for the impacted product line (primary responsibility: mitigation decisions, major comms)
- Bridge Operator: SRE on rotation (runs bridge, maintains timeline, posts updates)
- Customer Liaison: Customer Success rep or Solutions Engineer assigned for affected customers
- Legal & Security: Called in for incidents with data exposure or regulatory implications
- External Communications: Marketing/PR for elevated public statements

Service impact tiers (decision table):
1) Tier 0 — Informational
   - Symptom: Internal metric drift, non-customer-facing alert.
   - Action: Annotate dashboard, triage in regular backlog. No on-call invocation.
2) Tier 1 — Degraded but functional
   - Symptom: Increased latency, partial error rate affecting <5% customer traffic, SLA degradation risk.
   - Action: On-call alert -> Bridge if sustained >15 minutes. Customer status page update: optional.
3) Tier 2 — Partial outage
   - Symptom: Significant errors or latency affecting >=5% but <50% customers, feature-limited behavior.
   - Action: Immediate bridge, customer notification within 30 minutes, regular updates every 30 minutes.
4) Tier 3 — Major outage / data integrity risk
   - Symptom: Widespread failure or confirmed data exposure/corruption.
   - Action: Bridge immediately, IC to notify execs and Legal within 10 minutes, status page and customer emails within 15 minutes, hourly updates (or more frequent).

Callout and escalation protocol (step-by-step):
1. Detection (0 minutes): Monitoring or customer ticket triggers alert. Pager duty routes to the primary on-call for the service.
2. Acknowledge (0–2 minutes): On-call acknowledges via PD, posts to #ops-bridge with a short signal: "ACK — service-name — suspected-tier — initial-observations".
3. Assess (2–10 minutes): On-call runs quick triage checklist (below). If issue appears Tier 1 or above and persists >15 minutes, start bridge.
4. Bridge (start within 15 minutes for Tier 1+): Bridge created via Zoom/Google Meet + JIRA incident ticket created. Bridge link and ticket posted to #ops-bridge.
5. Assign IC (within first 5 minutes of bridge): If IC is not present the Bridge Operator nominates the IC and assigns primary Customer Liaison.
6. Customer comms decisions (within 15 minutes for Tier 2, within 15 minutes for Tier 3): Use templates below and post to status page and via direct customer channels.
7. Stabilize & Postmortem (post containment): IC declares the incident resolved or transitioned to remediation. Postmortem timeline starts (see "Postmortem and archival").

Triage checklist (commands & quick checks):
- Check global alerts: kubectl get pods, system metrics, autoscaler status, GPU queue length.
- Verify capacity/backpressure: redis queue depth, serving-runtime KV cache errors.
- Correlate deploys: check recent rollouts in Deployment dashboard and CI release notes.
- Authentication/permissions: check auth-service logs for 401 spikes.
- External dependencies: check third-party provider status pages.

On-call succession and handover rules:
- Shift length: Primary on-call is 8 hours (team policy), 4-week rotation cadence for primary owners.
- Succession: Outgoing on-call must hand over to incoming on-call on the bridge 10 minutes before shift end or create an explicit handoff message in #ops-bridge with: last-actions, known risks, mitigation toggles, and open actions list.
- Emergency transfer: If primary cannot continue, Bridge Operator escalates to secondary on-call and notifies the rotation lead.
- Shadowing & mentorship: New rotation members require two supervised shifts and one game day before independent primary assignments.

Game day playbook (quarterly):
- Objectives: validate callout flows, prove bridge creation automation, exercise customer comms, and verify postmortem cadence.
- Participants: SRE on-call, ICs from infra/serving/runtime/product, Customer Success, Legal (as needed), Observability owner.
- Format: 2-hour scenario, with simulated alerts and a forced deploy rollback. Observers score: bridge latency, comm latency, evidence quality.
- Scorecard thresholds: bridge created <15 min (pass), customer notice <30 min (pass), postmortem published <5 business days (pass).

Status page lifecycle and templates:
- Page states: Identified -> Investigating -> Mitigated -> Postmortem.
- Minimum status page content: impact scope, affected services, customer-facing workaround (if any), next update ETA.

Status page update template (short):
- Title: [Investigating] Service X increased error rate
- Body: We are investigating increased error rates for Service X affecting text generation for ~10% of requests. Our engineering team is collecting evidence and will provide an update by {ETA}.
- ETA cadence: 30 minutes for Tier 2, 15 minutes for Tier 3 until Mitigated.

Customer email template (initial notification):
- Subject: Incident: Service X degraded — {short timestamp UTC}
- Body: Hello {CustomerName},
  We detected elevated error rates impacting the Redwood inference API for some requests. Our engineers are investigating. We will provide updates via the status page and an estimated update at {ETA}. If you rely on dedicated capacity or have an active support contract, your Customer Liaison {LiaisonName} will reach out directly.
  - Impact: {short bullet}
  - Mitigation: {short bullet}
  - Next update: {ETA}
  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Operations Team

Escalation matrix quick reference (contact order):
1. Primary on-call -> 2. Secondary on-call -> 3. Bridge Operator -> 4. Service Owner/IC -> 5. SRE Manager -> 6. CTO (for Tier 3)

Postmortem and archival timeline (minimum required):
- Incident ticket created: immediate.
- Initial incident summary: within 24 hours.
- Full postmortem draft: within 5 business days, includes timeline, root cause, impact quantification, corrective actions, and owner for each action.
- Review: Postmortem review meeting within 7 business days with cross-functional attendees.
- Archive: Postmortem published to Confluence and linked on the status page record within 10 business days.

Postmortem template fields (must include):
- Title, Incident ID, Dates/times (UTC), Impacted services and customers, Detection path, Timeline (minute granularity), Root cause analysis, Corrective & preventive actions (owner + due date), Metrics change snapshots (graphs links), Lessons learned, and Follow-up verification plan.

Evidence capture checklist (during incident):
- Bridge transcript or meeting recording link
- PD acknowledgement logs and notes
- Key metrics snapshots with timestamps (CPU, GPU, latency, error rate)
- Relevant logs (trace IDs, request IDs) saved to incident ticket
- Customer impact list (customers affected, severity)

Retention and confidentiality rules:
- Postmortems are internal by default. If incident includes customer data or legal risk, mark confidentiality: restricted and follow Legal advice before external disclosure.
- Evidence artifacts retained in the incident ticket for 1 year.

Operational runbook references
- Runtime quick-restart (eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-restart-sop-2025)
- KV cache warmup and inspect (eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-recovery-2024)
- Autoscaler & capacity rollback (eng-infra/runbooks/autoscaler-rollback-guide-2025)

Appendix: Example Slack templates (internal)
- Bridge announce: "BRIDGE START — {service} — {tier} — bridge: {link} — IC: {name} — Liaison: {name} — initial-obs: {short}"
- Rapid update: "UPDATE — {service} — {elapsed} — action: {what we tried} — outcome: {result} — next ETA: {time}"

Appendix: Example public status page entry (JSON for automation)
- {
  "status": "investigating",
  "service": "inference.api.redwood",
  "impact": "Partial degradation — 10% requests",
  "update": "We are investigating increased error rates; next update at {ETA}"
}

Notes and governance:
- This protocol is reviewed annually and after every Tier 3 incident.
- Rotation leads are responsible for ensuring each new on-call completes the shadowing checklist.
- Exceptions to timing thresholds require explicit IC approval and must be recorded on the incident ticket.

Contact & escalation cheat-sheet: For immediate escalation, DM the on-call in PagerDuty, ping #exec-ops only after IC + SRE Manager consent.
